sentences.text: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of eleven players on a cricket field , at the centre of which is a rectangular 22-yard-long pitch with a wicket -LRB- a set of three wooden stumps -RRB- at each end .	bat-and-ball	bat-and-ball games	wicket	wicket	stumps	stump (cricket)	cricket field	cricket field	bat-and-ball game	bat-and-ball game	pitch	cricket pitch	field	fielding (cricket)	ball	cricket ball	bat	cricket bat
One team bats , attempting to score as many runs as possible , whilst their opponents field .	bats	batting (cricket)	runs	run (cricket)	field	fielding (cricket)
Each phase of play is called an innings .	innings	innings

After either ten batsmen have been dismissed or a fixed number of overs have been completed , the innings ends and the two teams then swap roles .	innings	innings	dismissed	dismissal (cricket)	overs	over (cricket)
The winning team is the one that scores the most runs , including any extras gained , during their innings .	runs	run (cricket)	innings	innings	scores	scoring (cricket)	extras	extra (cricket)
At the start of each game , two batsmen and eleven fielders enter the field of play .	field	fielding (cricket)

The play begins when a member of the fielding team , known as the bowler , delivers the ball from one end of the pitch to the other , towards the wicket at that end , in front of which stands one of the batsmen , known as the striker .	wicket	wicket	pitch	cricket pitch	bowler	bowling (cricket)	ball	cricket ball
The striker `` takes guard '' on a crease drawn on the pitch four feet in front of the wicket .	wicket	wicket	pitch	cricket pitch	crease	Crease (cricket)

His role is to prevent the ball from hitting the stumps by use of his bat , and simultaneously to strike it well enough to score runs .	stumps	stump (cricket)	runs	run (cricket)	ball	cricket ball	bat	cricket bat
The other batsman , known as the non-striker , waits at the opposite end of the pitch near the bowler .	pitch	cricket pitch	bowler	bowling (cricket)
A dismissed batsman must leave the field , and a teammate replaces him .	field	fielding (cricket)	dismissed	dismissal (cricket)
The bowler 's objectives are to prevent the scoring of runs and to dismiss the batsman .	runs	run (cricket)	bowler	bowling (cricket)
An over is a set of six deliveries bowled by the same bowler .	bowler	bowling (cricket)	deliveries	delivery (cricket)	bowled	bowled
The next over is bowled from the other end of the pitch by a different bowler .	pitch	cricket pitch	bowler	bowling (cricket)	bowled	bowled

The most common forms of dismissal are bowled , when the bowler hits the stumps directly with the ball ; leg before wicket , when the batsman prevents the ball from hitting the stumps with his body instead of his bat ; and caught , when the batsman hits the ball into the air and it is intercepted by a fielder before touching the ground .	wicket	wicket	stumps	stump (cricket)	bowler	bowling (cricket)	ball	cricket ball	bat	cricket bat	bowled	bowled	leg before wicket	leg before wicket	caught	caught

Runs are scored by two main methods : either by hitting the ball hard enough for it to cross the boundary , or by the two batsmen swapping ends by each simultaneously running the length of the pitch in opposite directions whilst the fielders are retrieving the ball .	pitch	cricket pitch	ball	cricket ball	boundary	boundary (cricket)

If a fielder retrieves the ball quickly enough to put down the wicket with a batsman not having reached the crease at that end of the pitch , that batsman is dismissed -LRB- a run-out occurs -RRB- .	wicket	wicket	pitch	cricket pitch	dismissed	dismissal (cricket)	ball	cricket ball	crease	Crease (cricket)	run-out	run-out
Adjudication is performed on the field by two umpires .	field	fielding (cricket)	umpires	umpire (cricket)

The laws of cricket are maintained by the International Cricket Council -LRB- ICC -RRB- and the Marylebone Cricket Club -LRB- MCC -RRB- .	International Cricket Council	International Cricket Council	laws of cricket	laws of cricket	Marylebone Cricket Club	Marylebone Cricket Club

There are various formats ranging from Twenty20 , played over a few hours with each team having a single innings of 20 overs -LRB- i.e. 120 deliveries -RRB- , to Test cricket , played over five days with unlimited overs and the teams playing two innings apiece .	innings	innings	overs	over (cricket)	deliveries	delivery (cricket)	Twenty20	Twenty20	Test cricket	Test cricket
Traditionally cricketers play in all-white kit , but in limited overs cricket they wear club or team colours .	overs	over (cricket)	limited overs cricket	limited overs cricket

In addition to the basic kit , some players wear protective gear to prevent injury caused by the ball , which is a hard , solid object made of compressed leather enclosing a cork core .	ball	cricket ball	protective gear	cricket clothing and equipment	leather	leather	cork	cork (material)
Although cricket 's origins are uncertain , it is first recorded in south-east England in the 16th century .
It spread globally with the expansion of the British Empire , leading to the first international matches in the mid-19th century .
ICC , the game 's governing body , has over 100 members , ten of which are full members who play Test cricket .	Test cricket	Test cricket	full members	List of International Cricket Council members
The sport is followed primarily in Australasia , Britain , the Indian subcontinent , southern Africa and the West Indies .	Australasia	Australasia	Indian subcontinent	Indian subcontinent
Women 's cricket , which is organised and played separately , has also achieved international standard .
